events.what: Nakanishi claims every connected vertex-transitive graph of odd order is Hamiltonian
events.credibility_reason: Several F5 signals together: v1 of 43KB cut to 3KB within a month over two revisions; no expert uptake in two years on a case that would be a landmark; three later papers on the same conjecture (2408.04618, 2505.08634, 2606.09742) neither cite it nor treat the odd-order case as settled.

events.what: Groenland, Longbrake, Steiner, Turcotte, Yepremyan raise the longest-cycle bound in vertex-transitive graphs to Ω(n^{13/21})
Norin, Steiner, Thomassé, Wollan raise the bound to Ω(n^{9/14})
Bedert, Draganić, Müyesser, Pavez-Signé prove the Lovász conjecture for Cayley graphs of degree d > n^{1-c}
Bucić, Christoph, Pokrovskiy, Steiner raise the bound to n^{2/3-o(1)}

judgement.doubts: Bedert et al. v1 date is given only by the arXiv identifier (March 2026); the record reports v2 on 20 Apr 2026. Setting Nakanishi aside as not_credible makes no difference to the codes: it would also be a case, at the same tier, with AI role none. arXiv:2505.05339 is about a different Lovász conjecture and is not counted here.

outcome_prefix: Bedert, Draganić, Müyesser and Pavez-Signé (arXiv:2603.08675, March 2026) prove the Lovász conjecture for Cayley graphs of degree d > n^{1-c}. This settles a restricted class of the conjecture.

corrections.why: F3/§4 step 3: the record's summary says arXiv:2603.08675 'proved the conjecture outright for a restricted regime', and that is a case. A case ranks above bound improvements, and competing_reading already argues this. Which activity is 'most-discussed' does not set the tier.
§4 step 6: a partial status carries the direction of the case it rests on, and that case proves what was conjectured.
F8: the status now rests on the Cayley-graph case, not on the n^{2/3-o(1)} bound.
